reason: Conversation 2's first reply correctly identified the likely cause (liquid/residue on the touch controls causing the hob to beep and cut out), gave the right sensible first step (isolate, wipe clean and dry, retry), was honest about not confirming the code, and set a reasonable 'engineer if it persists when dry' boundary. Conversation 1 opened with an unsupported overheat/ventilation diagnosis the customer had to correct, then responded with a generic water-near-plug stop panel that neither diagnosed the fault nor suited a hard-wired built-in hob. Conversation 2's second turn over-escalates (telling the owner not to use it even after drying until an engineer checks, and repeating the same plug/socket boilerplate), which costs it points, but it still served the homeowner far better than Conversation 1's misdiagnosis-then-panic path.
